driver.composition: The Controller generates an Authority signing keypair and per-Task authorized Online client keypairs. The reviewed host-create.go launcher uses CreateProcess with an OWNER RIGHTS SID (S-1-3-4) access-denied ACE covering STANDARD_RIGHTS_ALL and an explicit stdin/stdout/stderr handle list from process creation, so a same-SID sibling cannot acquire usable process handles before or after secret delivery. No post-start DACL change is relied upon. host-process-guard.mjs only proves readiness and receives secrets over the parent's stdin pipe, never environment files or command arguments. Authority and client public keys are Owner/FSW-bound by exact Task. Every request is RSA-SHA256 signed over canonical bytes of the complete protocol/version, recipient, request ID, operation, full value, CAS condition/expected revision and lease/capability identity; every response covers the complete result, revision and high-water identity. Offline creates and owns the canonical parent, empty SQLite registry and signed anchor and serves only the explicit bootstrap operations below. Production maintains an authorized-client registry: #370, future #284 and synthetic disjoint test Tasks use distinct per-Task keys with no shared private key, while unbound sibling keys remain denied. Temporary bytes are used once for #370 and retained only as read-only historical evidence; durable Authority/client behavior is implemented in host-resource-fence.mjs/test and consumed by single-writer.mjs/task-claim-github-publisher.mjs, never by silently retaining temporary code as production.
driver.credentialBoundary: Each selected process is created by host-create.go with an OWNER RIGHTS SID access-denied ACE and only three explicitly inherited stdio handles. An adversarial same-SID sibling racing from creation through secret delivery must fail to obtain VM read, VM write/operation, WRITE_DAC or duplicate handles. Only after those negatives does the parent pipe secrets: CodexSandboxOnline receives the GitHub token, real Octokit and its per-Task client private key, or CodexSandboxOffline receives the Authority private key. Public keys are Owner/FSW-bound by exact Task. Complete canonical request bytes are client-signed and complete result/revision/high-water bytes are Authority-signed. Ordinary Owner and Online have no protected-object write/WRITE_DAC/delete-child. Request files are add-only for Online and unreadable by other Online processes; production nonces encrypt to the authorized per-Task client public key. Same-SID siblings lack usable process handles and all relevant private keys, so key substitution, replay, forged response, process-memory access or file tamper cannot produce an accepted Host Claim. Before any live effect, inspect the actual Windows user-profile and GitHub credential surfaces visible to a same-SID unselected sibling and to historical drivers (including gh CLI/Git helpers, credential manager, process environment, files and inherited handles). Prove by read-only or disposable fake-transport adversarial tests that they cannot obtain or independently exercise a GitHub write credential accepted for the protected Issue, cannot use a non-fenced Octokit/HTTP writer and cannot recover a client private key. Clear inherited credential/config surfaces at launch; bind the selected token to the protected Online process only. If any alternative write-capable credential or unselected writer remains, this bootstrap is NOT_ISOLATED and must not post.

physicalDesign.authority: ONE_SHARED_SQLITE_CAS_FENCE_REGISTRY_DOCUMENT consulted by every current-source T06d/Native-C privileged Claim writer. The selected Host composition alone receives the registry mutation port and GitHub write transport; B/K/UI/Agent/request callers receive neither.
physicalDesign.productionComposition: A long-lived one-shot-per-operation CodexSandboxOffline Authority owns all registry and anchor mutation. CodexSandboxOnline transport/controller processes open only read facades and submit signed-protocol requests to that Authority. Native C rejects an absent/mismatched fence, the controller cannot publish without acquisition, and all repository callers including host-admission-source.test.mjs are migrated. The Offline-created protected objects grant no write/WRITE_DAC/delete-child to the ordinary Owner or Online SID; historical byte copies cannot open them for mutation and are never production entry points.
physicalDesign.credentialAndTransportBoundary: Selected processes are created with an OWNER RIGHTS SID access-denied ACE and explicit stdio handle list, then pass creation-race same-SID OpenProcess/handle negatives before receiving secrets through stdin. Only then does the selected Online process receive the GitHub token, real Octokit and its per-Task client private key, or the selected Offline Authority receive its private key. The authorized-client registry binds a distinct public key to each exact Task (#370, future #284 and synthetic test Tasks), enabling independently authorized concurrent contenders without shared private keys. Complete canonical request bytes (value, condition, expected revision, lease identity, recipient, operation and request ID) are client-signed; complete result/revision/high-water bytes are Authority-signed. Same-SID siblings lack usable process handles and all relevant private keys and cannot produce a valid accepted Claim; direct file tamper causes signed high-water verification to fail. Process-memory isolation does not by itself remove ambient authenticated GitHub access: the physical gate MUST test same-SID stale/unselected drivers against gh/Git credential helpers, Windows Credential Manager, inherited environment, profile files and handles, and verify they cannot POST directly with any other existing write token. Use a disposable transport for negative tests and NO live test POST. If a second actual writer can acquire a write-capable credential outside the selected guarded process, fail closed; token custody and all privileged transport entrances must be reconciled before accepting a shared-Host PASS.
physicalDesign.atomicity: The complete active-lease registry is one CAS document with a Host-configured registryId, mutated only by Offline Authority. Acquisition re-reads and validates the whole document, compares all exclusive resources and atomically adds one lease using mustBeAbsent for first initialization or mustMatchRevision thereafter. Claim/FSW store facades forward put conditions plus the current lease nonce; Authority validates key/phase/resource binding before executing them. At most 16 CAS retries are allowed; exhaustion returns HOST_RESOURCE_FENCE_CONTENTION_EXHAUSTED with zero Claim effect.
physicalDesign.continuousPossession: The random owner nonce is decrypted and retained only in the authorized per-Task Online process; CAS stores its SHA256 only. Every privileged stage sends canonical bytes covering protocol/version, recipient, fresh request ID, operation, expected identity, complete value and CAS condition/expected revision, signed by that Task's authorized client. Offline Authority re-reads registry/anchor, validates the authorized-client registry entry, registryId, fenceId, stable fenceRevision, nonce hash and exact binding, then signs the complete result/revision/high-water response. Leases never expire and no other writer can release without the nonce. The controller never releases during an in-flight effect, so protocol-compliant competitors cannot remove/reacquire between the final check and POST. Wrong-nonce release, overlapping acquisition, client-key substitution, request-value/condition tamper, replay, forged response or fabricated replacement denies.
physicalDesign.stableIdentity: fenceId and fenceRevision are assigned once at acquisition and never change when unrelated leases update the containing CAS row. The CAS row revision is a separate optimistic-concurrency value and is never serialized as the stable fenceRevision. fenceRevision equals the monotonically increasing registry generation at acquisition.
physicalDesign.lifetime: Definite pre-effect denial may release the still-owned lease. Successful publication and ambiguous/pending states retain it for Task ownership. Restarted processes do not receive the old nonce and cannot assert, release or reacquire the same resource set; recovery remains blocked pending native/CAS reconciliation. No automatic takeover or reset.
physicalDesign.registryRecreation: A null registry document is accepted only for the explicitly configured first initialization. Later null, changed registryId, generation regression, malformed document or deleted/recreated state is UNKNOWN and denies, never an empty-registry permit. The registry document itself is never deleted.
physicalDesign.rollbackAnchor: An independent append-only hash-and-signature chain anchor lives outside SQLite in the Offline-owned canonical parent and is writable only by Offline Authority. After every lease/Claim/FSW CAS, Authority computes the complete store snapshot (all keys, revisions and values), appends and fsyncs {registryId, generation, snapshotSha256, previousAnchorHash, writerSid} plus its RSA-SHA256 signature before any signed success or external effect. The expected current head is held in Authority process memory and checked before every operation; an Offline sibling cannot construct a new signed chain, and an unsigned/replayed/substituted chain fails. Authority restart never auto-recovers: with no in-memory expected head it refuses all operations and requires a separately reviewed Owner reconciliation, so restarted replay cannot grant access. Startup and every mutation also revalidate signatures, the complete chain and current generation/snapshot hash. CAS-success/anchor-failure, same-ID rollback, anchor-only truncation/replacement, generation regression or non-anchor mutation denies. The single Offline Authority MUST serialize the entire per-operation critical section (validated request, current complete-store read, public CAS mutation, fresh complete-store snapshot, next anchor link+fsync, signed full response) across every concurrently authorized client; a second mutation cannot interleave before the first durable anchor/ACK. No optimistic CAS success alone may be reported as stable. On pre-POST anchor failure, do not initiate any new external POST. On post-POST final CAS/anchor failure, acknowledge that the external GitHub event MAY already exist, retain the lease and exact pending/UNKNOWN evidence, re-read native state without blind POST retry and require reviewed reconciliation.
physicalDesign.publisherFence: Native C asserts the matching held lease immediately before and after each external POST. Omitting the port or using a mismatched/stale/lost lease prevents the POST or preserves pending evidence without retry. Fault injection at the transport boundary verifies the post-check/no-release invariant and uncertain-effect handling.
physicalDesign.resourceCompatibility: The PR #371 readHeldFence implementation derives compatibility from current durable foreign leases and their exact frozen resource objects, never from caller booleans or projected Claim fields. A foreign active Claim without a matching valid lease is incompatible. Snapshot drift retries only by re-running complete admission while still holding the lease; it never weakens conflict checks.

canonicalResourceContract.bytes: UTF-8 JSON.stringify of a recursive canonical value: plain object keys sorted by code unit; arrays retain semantic order except exclusive resource strings, which are sorted by code unit; undefined/functions/symbols/non-finite numbers/non-plain objects are rejected.
canonicalResourceContract.digest: frozenResourceSetSha256 = SHA256(canonicalBytes({schema, repository, issueRef, protectedClaimKey, generation, sourceSha, dispatchId, taskPackRef, taskPackBlobSha, reviewRef, ownerApprovalRef, writeSetSha256, exclusiveResources})). Recomputing the object must reproduce the port digest.
canonicalResourceContract.bindingVersusConflict: repository/issue/source/dispatch/Pack/review/Owner/write-set digest fields bind identity. Only normalized exclusiveResources participate in conflict comparison; metadata equality is still mandatory for possession.
canonicalResourceContract.file: Git repo-relative UTF-8 paths only: forward slashes, no empty/dot/dot-dot/backslash/drive/absolute/trailing-slash/NUL. Original Git spelling remains binding metadata. Conflict comparison uses the selected filesystem semantics: on the required Windows Host, paths are case-folded before exact/path-segment-ancestor comparison, so two Git paths differing only by case conflict and can never be declared disjoint; on case-sensitive Hosts the original case-sensitive comparison applies. Alias or unknown case/filesystem behavior denies.
canonicalResourceContract.cas: Exact validated CAS key string; only exact equality conflicts.
canonicalResourceContract.githubIssueComment: Canonical repository plus numeric Issue; the same Issue comment destination conflicts, different Issues are disjoint.
canonicalResourceContract.gitRef: Validated full refs/* name using code-unit comparison; exact or path-component ancestor ref conflicts.
canonicalResourceContract.gitWorktree: Only if a future Pack admits Agent effects: OS-canonical absolute realpath with Windows case folding, trailing separators removed and path-segment ancestor comparison. Alias, symlink, UNC/drive and ancestor negatives are mandatory before use.
canonicalResourceContract.unknown: Unknown resource types, duplicate/non-normalized resources or ambiguous path identity deny.
